title: Portable Eventstream definitions with verified pre-stream value-set activation
summary: Eventstream ALM definitions preserve symbolic connection/item/table references while runtime topology resolves IDs. Configure the target library first; fabio deploy verifies a reviewed value set before publishing dependent streams, halts on uncertainty and never switches strategy automatically.
authoring: Use properties.connectionReference or properties.itemReference with literal syntax $(/**/LibraryName/VariableName). Some contracts support tableNameReference/tableNamesReference. Do not mix a reference with non-null resolved dataConnectionId, workspaceId/itemId or tableName/tableNames fields.

Support is connector- and property-specific. CustomEndpoint, Cribl and SAPDatasphere have no reference properties in the published matrix. Eventhouse/Lakehouse/Activator/Notebook/BusinessEvents destinations have itemReference support; Eventhouse also has tableNameReference. Inspect the linked matrix before authoring other contracts.

An Eventhouse itemReference targets the receiving KQL DATABASE, not its parent Eventhouse. ProcessedIngestion still needs inputSerialization and tableName or tableNameReference. Keep source-specific properties such as consumer groups and serialization.

Get Definition and Git contain symbolic references. Runtime topology exposes resolved IDs, not the same portable authored representation. Never export topology as a replacement definition or substitute identifiers into symbolic strings.

ReferenceLakehouse retains absoluteOneLakePath table selection and refresh options; LakehouseChangeFeed retains table selection or tableNamesReference. Fabio does not invent/rewrite paths or selections from a variable. Verify resolved runtime paths and columns against the intended source.
Variable libraries store pointers to managed resources, not credentials. Keep secrets in connections; never put tokens, passwords or connection strings in source control or text variables.
deployment: Configure target value-set pointers before consumer publication. Include required VariableLibrary items in the scoped source/plan; unchanged skipped libraries are supported. Fabio does not inventory/select a different library implicitly.

Item references are static workspace/item pointers, not instructions to discover or construct future IDs. For first-time targets, stage destination/connection creation first and explicitly configure the target value set with those returned IDs. Do not assume one-pass deployment automatically fixes every advanced variable value.

Reference-bearing stream changes (or library changes affecting source-bundle streams) require reviewed --env <VALUE_SET>, default/sequential strategy and hooks enabled. Bulk cannot activate a library between imports. Do not guess an environment, switch strategy or remove guards automatically; review a staged plan.

deploy apply --dry-run shows variableLibraryPrerequisites with verified:false and a destructive signal. Execution checks target variable existence and the requested value-set part, activates if necessary, reads back the exact active set, then publishes dependent streams. pre_stream records retain successful/failed activations; uncertainty halts later mutations and forbids batch replay.
Already-active reviewed sets need no PATCH. Failed library deployment blocks consumers. Verified pre-stream activations are not repeated by the optional final activation hook.

Value-set changes can affect existing consumers immediately. This is not an atomic cutover and fabio does not pause running streams. Review affected consumers and coordinate operational changes separately.

Configuration/active-set checks do not prove source credentials, destination authorization, source availability or event delivery. Compare authored definition and resolved topology, then separately approve/send scoped synthetic events and query the intended destination before declaring end-to-end readiness.
